questions.q: According to the summary, what makes personal boundaries harder to enforce than physical ones?
a: Other people cannot see where they are
They only apply inside the home
They disappear once you reach work
They must be approved by a therapist
questions.why: Lesson 1 contrasts visible fences and signs with personal boundaries, which protect your emotions and spirit but are invisible to others.

questions.q: In the O'Riley family example, what would count as a healthy boundary?
a: Supporting their son without fixing his problems
Paying his fines and choosing a new school
Refusing to speak to him until he apologizes
Letting him handle the family finances
questions.why: Lesson 1 says the parents can listen and support Peter's recovery while leaving responsibility for his problems with him.

questions.q: Which feeling does the summary describe as a useful signal that a boundary has been violated too long?
a: Resentment
Nostalgia
Boredom
Curiosity
questions.why: Lesson 2 says resentment can be a good thing when it shows you are finished being complacent about boundary violations.

questions.q: Why does the summary say controlling people can feel addictive to someone who complies with them?
a: Their demands make the compliant person feel needed
They offer clear rewards for good behavior
They remove all need to make decisions
They are usually more affectionate than friends
questions.why: Lesson 2 explains that a controller's insistence on using you creates a high, which friends who accept a simple no do not provide.

questions.q: What does the summary say about boundaries in a professional setting?
a: Being at work does not mean your boundaries vanish
Boundaries should be suspended while you are on the clock
Only managers are entitled to set limits
Work boundaries matter less than personal ones
questions.why: Lesson 3 stresses that boundaries are just as important at work, including not taking responsibility for colleagues' poor performance.
